note: Both sets contain the same six claims with identical values, conditions, and quotes; the only differences are cosmetic (A keeps the Θpitch symbol in two attribute names and orders the claims differently). Both correctly bind the 4° maximum pitch to low wind speeds/Region 1.5, the ~90 m force peak to below-rated wind speeds, and the design (TSR 9.0, Θpitch 0°) versus optimal (TSR 8.5, Θpitch −1.0°) points to the right blade properties. Neither set has a misread, misbound, or invented claim, so they are effectively equivalent.
remarks: Both sets drop the 'approximately' qualifier on the 90 m force-peak location (minor). Both also omit other engineering facts on the page, e.g. the sharp linear force drop over the outboard 5% of the blade caused by the Prandtl tip loss model, and Region 3 behavior (torque saturated at rated torque, pitch to feather to maintain rated rotor speed); since both sets show all their claims, these are missing from both equally.
